flawed_step: Step 1: any attempt to bound the chromatic number of a triangle-free graph by 4 cannot be justified. Being triangle-free limits clique size, not chromatic number (the Mycielski construction gives triangle-free graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number).
counterexample: The Mycielskian of the Grötzsch graph (23 vertices, 71 edges). Mycielskian M(G): keep G on v1..vn, add u1..un with ui adjacent to the G-neighbours of vi, and add w adjacent to all ui. (A) If G is triangle-free, so is M(G): the u's are independent; w meets only u's; a triangle ui-vj-vk would give the triangle vi-vj-vk in G. (B) chi(M(G)) >= chi(G)+1: given a proper k-colouring with k = chi(G), rename colours so w has colour k; then no ui has colour k. Recolour each colour-k vertex vi with c(ui). This is proper on G: colour-k vertices are independent, and a neighbour vj of vi has c(vj) != k and c(vj) != c(ui) because vj ~ ui. So G would be (k-1)-colourable, a contradiction. Chain: K2 (chi 2) -> M(K2) = C5 (chi 3) -> Grötzsch graph H = M(C5) (11 vertices: 5-cycle a0..a4, b_i ~ a_{i-1}, a_{i+1}, z ~ all b_i; chi 4) -> M(H): add copies x' for each x in H with x' ~ the H-neighbours of x, plus t ~ all x'. M(H) is triangle-free with chi >= 5, so it is not 4-colourable.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. Iterating the Mycielski construction keeps graphs triangle-free and raises the chromatic number by 1 each time. From K2 it gives C5, then the Grötzsch graph (chi 4), then a 23-vertex triangle-free graph with chromatic number 5, which is not 4-colourable.
